ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the horizontal axis is years AD, and there are two main curves in the figure. The solid line represents the sedimentation rate of the downstream river channel, and the dashed/dotted line represents the climate humidity index of the middle reaches of the Yellow River. It can be seen that between AD 600 and 1100, the solid line as a whole rises noticeably and reaches a relatively high level, while the dashed/dotted line overall shows a declining or relatively low state. Then reason: a significant increase in sedimentation rate usually means intensified erosion and increased sediment transport; if the climate humidity index in the same period does not rise synchronously, but instead is relatively low or declines, it is more likely to indicate that vegetation degradation in the middle reaches led to intensified soil erosion. From this, it is judged that before the 19th century, the period that best reflects severe vegetation degradation in the middle reaches of the Yellow River is AD 600~1100.

raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: the horizontal axis is years AD, and there are two main curves in the figure. The solid line represents the sedimentation rate of the downstream river channel, and the dashed/dotted line represents the climate humidity index of the middle reaches of the Yellow River. It can be seen that between AD 600 and 1100, the solid line as a whole rises noticeably and reaches a relatively high level, while the dashed/dotted line overall shows a declining or relatively low state. Then reason: a significant increase in sedimentation rate usually means intensified erosion and increased sediment transport; if the climate humidity index in the same period does not rise synchronously, but instead is relatively low or declines, it is more likely to indicate that vegetation degradation in the middle reaches led to intensified soil erosion. From this, it is judged that before the 19th century, the period that best reflects severe vegetation degradation in the middle reaches of the Yellow River is AD 600~1100.
